overall_assessment: Strong, faithful implementation of the design. Layering is clean (services own DB access and raise AppError, routers serialize, deps enforce authz), the NFR-3 uniqueness story is correctly DB-backed with IntegrityError->409 rather than read-modify-write, aggregations are single GROUP BY statements, the one-active-pulse partial unique index is present, and quiz correct-answer secrecy is enforced (PollOptionOut omits is_correct; a test asserts absence). Auth 401/403, double-submit 409, lifecycle guards, join enforcement, and pulse sentiment are all implemented and tested. Env-fixture contract PASSES: both src/.env.example (keys only, all 9 documented) and src/.env.test (schema-valid values: 38-char JWT_SECRET >= min_length 32, sqlite:///:memory: DATABASE_URL, valid LOG_LEVEL/LOG_JSON enums, JOIN_CODE_LENGTH within 6..12) exist and are internally consistent with the pydantic-settings schema in app/config.py. Tests pass 24/24 at 89.6% coverage. One MAJOR correctness deviation: every list endpoint returns a bare JSON array instead of the design-mandated {"items": [...]} envelope. Remaining items are minor/nit. Recommend fixing the list-envelope deviation; the minors are low-risk.

findings.issue: API contract deviation: design section 3 specifies every list endpoint returns {"items": [...]} (GET /courses, GET /courses/{id}/enrollments, GET /courses/{id}/sessions, GET /sessions/{id}/participants, GET /sessions/{id}/questions). The implementation returns bare arrays via response_model=list[...]. common.py was specified to hold list wrappers but none exists. A client coded to the spec breaks on all five list endpoints. Tests were written to the bare-array shape, so this is not caught.
findings.fix: Add a generic ItemsOut wrapper (or per-resource ItemsOut) in schemas/common.py and have each list route return {"items": [...]}; update the five list routes' response_model and the corresponding test assertions.

findings.issue: get_current_principal constructs Principal(subject=payload['sub'], role=payload['role']) OUTSIDE the try/except. decode_token's required-claims option only requires exp/iss/sub, not role. A validly-signed token lacking a 'role' claim raises KeyError, which escapes as an uncaught 500 instead of a 401.
findings.fix: Read role via payload.get('role') inside the guarded block and raise AuthError(UNAUTHORIZED, 'Invalid token') if sub or role is missing, so malformed-but-signed tokens yield 401.

findings.issue: trigger_pulse closes the prior active pulse then inserts a new active pulse but does not wrap the flush in try/except IntegrityError. The one-active-pulse partial unique index is the DB-backed invariant per design 2.12; a concurrent double-trigger would raise IntegrityError -> uncaught 500 rather than the intended 409. Low likelihood because the route is owner-only, but the design explicitly relies on the index and the ADR-8.4 IntegrityError->409 pattern is used everywhere else.
findings.fix: Catch IntegrityError around the new-pulse flush, rollback, and raise ConflictError with a stable code (e.g. 'pulse_conflict') to mirror the other insert paths.

findings.issue: DATABASE_URL validator only checks v.startswith('sqlite'); design section 6 requires it start with 'sqlite:///' or 'sqlite+pysqlite:///'. Values like 'sqlitefoo' pass validation. Loose vs the declared contract.
findings.fix: Tighten the validator to require one of the sqlite:/// or sqlite+pysqlite:/// prefixes.

findings.issue: Layering rule (design 1.2: 'No SQL in routers') is bent: _poll_out issues db.query(PollOption) directly and /auth/me issues db.query(User) in the router. Functionally correct but reads belong in a service/aggregation helper.
findings.fix: Move the option lookup and user lookup into service functions; routers should only serialize.

findings.issue: submit_rating raises ConflictError with a bare literal 'pulse_closed' instead of a named constant, inconsistent with the error-code constants centralized in errors.py.
findings.fix: Add a POLL/ PULSE_CLOSED constant to errors.py and reference it.

findings.issue: pydantic-settings env_file is '.env' (not '.env.test'); .env.test satisfies the greenfield fixture contract but is not auto-loaded by config.py. Tests instead rely on os.environ.setdefault in conftest.py, and a real .env file is present in the working tree. Contract is met (file exists and is schema-valid), but the .env.test values are not exercised by the app boot path.
findings.fix: Optional: document that .env.test is the canonical test fixture and/or point tests at it explicitly; ensure .env is gitignored so no dev secret is committed.

findings.issue: Design 4.7 access-log line includes optional actor_subject; the emitted line omits it (only method/path/status/duration/request_id). No PII leak; just a missing optional field.
findings.fix: Optionally attach actor_subject to the access log extra when a principal is resolved.

refinement_packets.instruction: Introduce an items-envelope for all list endpoints to match design section 3. Add a reusable wrapper in schemas/common.py (e.g. a generic ItemsOut[T] or explicit CourseListOut/EnrollmentListOut/SessionListOut/ParticipantListOut/QuestionListOut) and change these routes to return {"items": [...]}: GET /courses, GET /courses/{course_id}/enrollments, GET /courses/{course_id}/sessions, GET /sessions/{session_id}/participants, GET /sessions/{session_id}/questions. Update response_model on each. Update tests in test_courses.py, test_sessions.py, test_questions.py that currently read bare arrays to read from the .items key. Keep single-object routes unchanged.

In get_current_principal (src/app/deps/auth.py) resolve both sub and role via payload.get(...) inside the guarded block and raise AuthError(UNAUTHORIZED, 'Invalid token') if either is missing, so a validly-signed token lacking the role claim returns 401 instead of an uncaught 500. Add a unit test that mints/crafts a token without a role claim and asserts 401.

In trigger_pulse (src/app/services/pulse.py) wrap the new-active-pulse insert flush in try/except IntegrityError, rollback, and raise ConflictError with a stable code so a concurrent double-trigger colliding on the one-active-pulse partial unique index returns 409 rather than 500, consistent with ADR-8.4. Add a stable error-code constant in errors.py.

env_fixture_check.notes: Both files exist under src/. .env.example documents all 9 keys with no values. .env.test supplies schema-valid values (JWT_SECRET is 38 chars >= min_length 32; DATABASE_URL sqlite:///:memory:; LOG_LEVEL WARNING; LOG_JSON false; JOIN_CODE_LENGTH 8 within 6..12; JWT_EXPIRES_SECONDS 3600 within 60..86400). Consistent with the pydantic-settings Settings schema in app/config.py.
